brief:
The International Court of Justice ruled for the first time that a state bears direct responsibility for genocide, finding Myanmar culpable in the persecution of its Rohingya Muslim minority, Mondoweiss reported. The landmark decision establishes a legal precedent for holding governments accountable for mass atrocities at the highest judicial level.

The ruling raises questions about potential accountability for Israel's conduct in Gaza, where rights groups and observers have documented mass casualties and destruction. Whether the ICJ will apply similar standards to alleged Israeli actions remains uncertain, though the Myanmar judgment establishes that genocide findings against states are judicially possible.
dek: For the first time in history, the ICJ has found a state directly guilty of genocide. It remains to be seen if Israel's genocide in Gaza will follow.
title: ICJ finds Myanmar guilty of genocide in historic ruling
